extracted.intended_audience: researchers, industry and university partners, and potential proposers interested in DARPA I2O-funded R&D (AI, software, cyber) for national security
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the Information Innovation Office's stated technical priorities, expectations, and engagement modes that proposals or collaborations should align with. Useful for proposers and partners who want to target DARPA I2O programs in AI, secure software, and cyber capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformative AI: invent trustworthy, disruptive AI relevant to national security
rubrics_metrics.description: We seek to invent trustworthy, disruptive AI technologies and methodologies relevant to national security that no one else will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority for work that is both disruptive and unique (i.e., capabilities others do not have) and that directly addresses national-security needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of trustworthy systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Trustworthy systems are defined as ones that operate competently, interact appropriately with humans and behave ethically and morally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target systems meeting these three facets (competence, appropriate human interaction, ethical/moral behavior) rather than only raw performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resilient, adaptable, and secure software via formal methods and third-wave AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Use formal methods and third-wave AI to make it easier to understand, build, update, repair, and restore complex software and cyber-physical systems with multi-system-wide, security-relevant correctness guarantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should produce techniques that improve comprehensibility and correctness guarantees across systems; emphasis on system-wide, security-relevant correctness rather than only component fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver techniques and tools as open-source for broad adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques and tools are provided as open-source software for use by the research and software development communities, the defense industrial base, and DOD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for outputs that are shareable/open-source to accelerate adoption by academia, industry, and defense stakeholders; consider reproducibility and distribution plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage state-of-the-art AI and secure/resilient tools for cyber capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage advances in state-of-the-art AI and secure and resilient tools and technologies to produce trustworthy cyber capabilities that operate beyond human capacity and speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed cyber capabilities should exploit AI to exceed human operational tempo and scale while preserving trustworthiness and resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate adversary countermeasures
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts should anticipate adversary countermeasures to create enduring capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and evaluation should consider likely adversary responses and adapt to ensure long-term effectiveness rather than one-off wins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on measuring, protecting, and detecting attacks in the information domain
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on measuring the health of and protecting and detecting attacks on the information domain, broadly construed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should address integrity/availability/confidentiality of information across multiple dimensions rather than only narrow network aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address multi-level information-domain research areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Research portfolio spans many levels: Cognitive (beliefs and attitudes); Semantic (knowledge specialized to particular domains); Tracking (recording digital artifacts of interactions); Transport (delivery of electronic messages in many forms and with various gradations of observability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should clarify which information-domain level(s) they target and how methods or systems apply at that level; cross-level approaches are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-risk, high-reward research with finite-duration programs and lasting impact
rubrics_metrics.description: I2O research programs are finite in duration, but the revolutionary advancements they drive create lasting change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should aim for radical/transformative outcomes that can produce lasting transition despite program time limits; emphasize path to durable impact/transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement modes: R&D programs, challenge competitions, and technology transition efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities to engage include R&D programs and efforts, challenge competitions, and technology transition efforts for the Information Innovation Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should align their mode of engagement (basic/advanced R&D, challenges, or transition activities) with program solicitations and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas under incubation: solicit missing contextual information via stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Before an idea becomes a program, program managers talk extensively to experts, potential transition partners, and each other to identify what information is missing for program development and invite external input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early-stage idea engagement is iterative and consultative; contributors should provide concrete insights or missing context that help shape potential programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium-building and partnerships to accelerate adoption (AI FORGE example)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI FORGE aims to establish an industry/university/government consortium on AI research focused on solving AI critical challenges for national security, with the goal of accelerating adoption by industry and federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for multi-sector partnerships and consortium approaches that plan for technology adoption and scaling across government and industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program manager leadership and visionary expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: I2O program managers are described as visionary leaders whose experience spans industry, government, and academia and who conceive, plan, and oversee high-risk R&D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate how they align with program manager visions and provide clear plans that address the program's strategic aims and practical oversight/transition considerations.
